architecture.mechanism: A non-contact temperature sensor detects the temperature of each area of the heating chamber, enabling per-zone monitoring that can be used to modulate microwave and radiant heat inputs so hot spots are reduced and cold centers are brought up to temperature.
architecture.intervention: Add an infrared (non-contact) temperature sensor array to the microwave cavity that maps surface temperature across the food in real time, and couple it to a control loop that reduces microwave power (or activates radiant/convective heating) in zones detected as overheating while continuing to heat zones detected as cold, using a mode-stirrer or turntable to redistribute energyâall without user intervention.
architecture.expected_effect: Hot spots at food edges stop burning while cold centers reach target temperature, producing substantially more uniform heating within a single automatic cycle.
architecture.falsification_test: Place a tray of uniform food (e.g., mashed potato or gel) in the oven, run a fixed cycle with the sensor-based zoning active, and immediately measure a thermal map with an infrared camera; repeat with zoning disabled. The intervention is falsified if the active configuration does not significantly reduce the max-to-min temperature spread (e.g., no reduction toward a target like ÎT < 10Â°C) or if edges still exceed a burn threshold while the center remains below the target.
